response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS n FROM rental re JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = re.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg_n FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.n) AS avg_rentals_above_avg_ratings, AVG(r.n - a.avg_n) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM r CROSS JOIN a WHERE r.n > a.avg_n

assumptions.assumption: 'How much a rating gets rented' means the total number of rental rows per rating (rental -> inventory -> film). Ratings are the 5 levels in film.rating.

The 'average across ratings' is the unweighted mean of the 5 per-rating rental counts. The 'how far above' figure is the mean of (rating count minus that overall mean) among the ratings that exceed it.
